extracted.intended_audience: corporate issuers, investor_relations, CFOs, securities lawyers, and compliance officers preparing press releases and other public financial disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for presenting non-GAAP financial measures in press releases, earnings materials, and SEC filings consistent with Regulation G and Item 10(e) of Regulation S-K. Focuses on when measures are misleading, labeling, reconciliation, prominence, and specific measure types (EBIT/EBITDA, free cash flow, segment info, forecasts, business combination communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments that could render a non-GAAP measure misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain adjustments, although not explicitly prohibited, may cause the presentation of a non-GAAP measure to be misleading and violate Rule 100(b) of Regulation G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an adjustment is misleading depends on individual facts and circumstances. Example: excluding normal, recurring, cash operating expenses necessary to run the business could be misleading. Staff considers nature and effect of the adjustment and how it relates to operations, revenue-generating activities, business strategy, industry and regulatory environment. Operating expenses that occur repeatedly or occasionally (even irregularly) are viewed as recurring. [Dec. 13, 2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of presentation between periods
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP measure can be misleading if presented inconsistently between periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusting a particular charge or gain in the current period while not adjusting similar prior-period items could violate Rule 100(b) unless the change is disclosed and reasons explained. Significant changes may require recasting prior measures to conform with current presentation and providing appropriate context. [May 17, 2016]

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusting charges but not gains
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP measure that excludes charges but does not exclude gains may be misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: adjusting only for non-recurring charges when non-recurring gains occurred in the same period could violate Rule 100(b). [May 17, 2016]

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with GAAP recognition and measurement principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-GAAP adjustments that change the recognition or measurement principles required by GAAP may be individually tailored and misleading under Rule 100(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: accelerating GAAP-recognized ratable revenue to recognize when billed; presenting revenue net when GAAP requires gross (or vice versa); changing from accrual to cash basis for revenue or expenses. Such changes are likely misleading. [Dec. 13, 2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate labeling and clear description
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP measure or any adjustment must be appropriately labeled and clearly described; otherwise it can be misleading and violate Rule 100(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations include failing to identify a measure as non-GAAP; using a label that mischaracterizes the measure (e.g., calling a contribution margin 'net revenue'); labeling a non-GAAP measure the same as a GAAP line item even though calculated differently (e.g., 'Gross Profit' or 'Sales'); labeling a non-GAAP measure 'pro forma' when it does not meet Article 11 Regulation S-X pro forma requirements. [Dec. 13, 2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure limits do not always cure misleading measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive, detailed disclosure about the nature and effect of adjustments may not prevent a non-GAAP measure from being materially misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff may view a non-GAAP measure as so misleading that even comprehensive disclosure cannot prevent material misleadingness. [Dec. 13, 2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial measures in forecasts for financial advisors (business combinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial measures included in forecasts provided to a financial advisor and used in connection with a business combination are not non-GAAP financial measures if specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 10(e)(5) of Regulation S-K and Rule 101(a)(3) of Regulation G exclude measures required to be disclosed by GAAP, Commission rules, or an applicable regulatory system. Measures provided to a financial advisor are excluded if (1) included in forecasts provided to the advisor for rendering an opinion materially related to the transaction, and (2) forecasts are disclosed to comply with Item 1015 of Regulation M-A or applicable state/foreign law regarding disclosure of the advisor's analyses/work. [Oct. 17, 2017]

rubrics_metrics.name: Same forecasts provided to board of directors
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant may rely on the exclusion for forecasts provided to a financial advisor even if the same forecasts are provided to the board or a board committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer: Yes. [Apr. 4, 2018]

rubrics_metrics.name: Forecasts exchanged among bidders in business combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: If registrant determines forecasts exchanged between parties in a business combination are material and must be disclosed to comply with federal anti-fraud or related requirements, the financial measures in such forecasts are excluded from non-GAAP treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such measures would not be subject to Item 10(e) of Regulation S-K or Regulation G if disclosed for those purposes. [Apr. 4, 2018]

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for communications under certain transaction rules does not extend to registration/proxy/tender statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The exemption from Regulation G and Item 10(e) for non-GAAP measures in communications relating to business combinations (e.g., Rule 425, Rules 14a-12, 14d-2(b)(2), 14d-9(a)(2)) does not extend to registration statements, proxy statements, or tender offer statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the same non-GAAP measure appears in a registration or proxy/tender statement, the exemption is not available for that disclosure. [Oct. 17, 2017]

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pro forma measures for reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the most directly comparable GAAP measure is a 'pro forma' measure prepared under Article 11 of Regulation S-X, companies may use that measure for reconciliation in lieu of a GAAP financial measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer: Yes. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: FFO reference and acceptable definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to 'funds from operations' (FFO) in SEC guidance refers to NAREIT's definition as of specified dates; the staff accepts NAREIT's definition in effect as of May 17, 2016 for presentation as a performance measure and per share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NAREIT revised/clarified definitions since 2000; staff acceptance is to the definition in effect as of May 17, 2016. [May 17, 2016]

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenting FFO on other bases
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may present FFO on a basis other than NAREIT's May 17, 2016 definition provided adjustments comply with Item 10(e) and do not violate Rule 100(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments must comply with Item 10(e) requirements for performance or liquidity measures. Some adjustments may trigger prohibition on presenting the measure on a per share basis. See Section 100 and Question 102.05. [May 17, 2016]

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on labeling items as non-recurring based on nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition against adjusting a performance measure to eliminate or smooth items identified as non-recurring/infrequent/unusual when such items are reasonably likely to recur within two years (or similar charge/gain occurred in prior two years) is based on the description of the charge/gain being adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant should not label an item 'non-recurring, infrequent or unusual' unless it meets specified criteria. Not being able to describe an item as non-recurring does not mean the registrant cannot adjust for it — but adjustments remain subject to Regulation G and Item 10(e). See Question 100.01. [May 17, 2016]

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement that management use the non-GAAP measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant is not required to use a non-GAAP measure in managing its business to be able to disclose it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 10(e)(1)(i)(D) requires disclosure of additional purposes for which management uses the measure 'to the extent material' and 'if any' — but does not prohibit disclosing a non-GAAP measure not used by management. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Per share non-GAAP measures: performance vs liquidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-GAAP per share performance measures may be meaningful and are not categorically prohibited, but non-GAAP liquidity measures that measure cash generated must not be presented on a per share basis in documents filed or furnished with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether per share presentation is prohibited depends on whether the measure is a liquidity measure in substance, not management's characterization. Non-GAAP per share performance measures should be reconciled to GAAP EPS. Staff focuses on substance over label. [May 17, 2016]

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of statement of cash flows categories with liquidity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: When a non-GAAP liquidity measure is presented, registrant should present amounts for the three major categories of the statement of cash flows consistent with staff practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 10(e)(1)(i) requirements are consistent with staff practice; the three major categories should be presented when a non-GAAP liquidity measure is shown. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Free cash flow presentation and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting 'free cash flow' as cash flows from operating activities less capital expenditures is not prohibited, but the measure lacks uniform definition and its title does not describe its calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies should clearly describe how free cash flow is calculated and provide necessary reconciliation. Avoid implying it represents residual cash available for discretionary expenditures when mandatory obligations exist. Free cash flow is a liquidity measure and must not be presented on a per share basis. See Question 102.05. [May 17, 2016]

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Item 10(e) to free writing prospectuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e) applies to registration statements and Exchange Act filings; a free writing prospectus is not part of a registration statement unless filed on Form 8-K or incorporated by reference, so Item 10(e) does not apply to a free writing prospectus unless included in or incorporated into a registration or Exchange Act filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on excluding cash-settlement charges from non-GAAP liquidity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e)(1)(ii)(A) prohibits excluding charges or liabilities that required or will require cash settlement from non-GAAP liquidity measures, other than EBIT and EBITDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-GAAP measure (e.g., Adjusted EBITDA used in a credit covenant) excludes cash-settlement charges, presenting it in filings would violate Item 10(e). However, MD&A may require disclosure of such measures if the credit agreement/covenant is material to understanding liquidity; in that case, company may disclose the covenant-based measure but should also disclose the material terms of the credit agreement, covenant limits, and actual/or reasonably likely effects of compliance or non-compliance on financial condition and liquidity. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence: GAAP measure equal or greater prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting a non-GAAP measure registrants must present the most directly comparable GAAP measure with equal or greater prominence to avoid giving undue prominence to the non-GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of non-GAAP prominence include: presenting a non-GAAP income statement; presenting non-GAAP before or omitting the comparable GAAP measure (including headlines); presenting ratios using non-GAAP without GAAP-based ratios; emphasizing non-GAAP via style (bold/larger font); describing non-GAAP as 'record' without equal GAAP characterization; presenting charts/tables/graphs of non-GAAP without comparable GAAP with equal prominence; providing discussion/analysis of non-GAAP without similar GAAP analysis in equally prominent location. [Dec. 13, 2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation prominence pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: There are examples of disclosures that would cause the non-GAAP reconciliation to give undue prominence to a non-GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: starting the reconciliation with a non-GAAP measure; presenting a non-GAAP income statement when reconciling; when relying on forward-looking reconciliation exception, failing to disclose reliance, what info is unavailable, and its probable significance in equally prominent location. [Dec. 13, 2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a non-GAAP income statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-GAAP income statement is one comprised of non-GAAP measures that includes all or most line items and subtotals found in a GAAP income statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff considers presenting such a non-GAAP income statement (alone or as part of reconciliation) to give undue prominence to non-GAAP measures. [Dec. 13, 2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Income tax effects on non-GAAP adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants should present income tax effects related to adjustments to arrive at a non-GAAP measure depending on the nature of the measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If measure is liquidity and includes income taxes, adjusting GAAP taxes to show taxes paid in cash might be acceptable. If a performance measure, include current and deferred income tax expense commensurate with the non-GAAP profitability measure. Adjustments should not be presented 'net of tax'; income taxes should be shown as a separate adjustment and clearly explained. [May 17, 2016]

rubrics_metrics.name: Information prepared under other governmental or self-regulatory guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial information not in accordance with GAAP but prepared under guidance published by a government, governmental authority, or self-regulatory organization is a non-GAAP financial measure for Regulation G and Item 10 if not required disclosure by that regulator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information must comply with Regulation G/Item 10 disclosures, including quantitative reconciliation to the most comparable GAAP measure, with sufficient detail to allow reader to understand reconciling items. [Apr. 24, 2009]

rubrics_metrics.name: EBIT and EBITDA definitions and acceptable labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: EBIT means 'earnings before interest and taxes' and EBITDA means 'earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization', where 'earnings' refers to net income as presented under GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures calculated differently than those described should not be labeled 'EBIT' or 'EBITDA' and should have distinguished titles (e.g., 'Adjusted EBITDA'). Such differently calculated measures are not exempt from Item 10(e)(1)(ii)(A)'s prohibition, except as addressed in Question 102.09. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation target for EBIT/EBITDA when presented as performance measures
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting EBIT or EBITDA as a performance measure, reconcile to net income as presented in the statement of operations under GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating income is not the most directly comparable GAAP measure because EBIT/EBITDA adjust for items not included in operating income. These measures must not be presented on a per share basis. [May 17, 2016]

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment information conforming with ASC 280 is not a non-GAAP measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment profit/loss and total assets presented in conformity with ASC 280 are not non-GAAP financial measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASC 280 measures reported to the chief operating decision maker and required to be disclosed under GAAP are excluded from Regulation G/Item 10(e)'s definition. The release's list of examples is not exclusive; footnote-required segment disclosures are also excluded. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: MD&A discussion of ASC 280 segment information
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 10(e)(1)(ii) does not prohibit discussion in MD&A of segment information determined in conformity with ASC 280.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including segment profitability determined consistent with ASC 280 in MD&A, also include a complete discussion of reconciling items that apply to the particular segment; see Financial Reporting Codification Section 501.06.a, footnote 28. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment measures not in conformity with ASC 280 are non-GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment measures adjusted to include or exclude amounts differing from the amounts reported to the chief operating decision maker under ASC 280 are non-GAAP measures and subject to Regulation G and Item 10(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such adjusted segment profit/loss or liquidity measures do not comply with ASC 280 and therefore are non-GAAP. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of total segment profit/loss outside ASC 280 footnote is non-GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: Totaling profit or loss for individual segments and presenting that total outside the ASC 280-required footnote reconciliation constitutes presenting a non-GAAP financial measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The total segment profit/loss has no authoritative meaning outside the ASC 280 footnote reconciliation and thus is a non-GAAP presentation if shown elsewhere. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakdowns of revenue by product are not non-GAAP if GAAP-compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: A table showing product revenue breakdowns that does not sum to the consolidated revenue is not a non-GAAP financial measure if the product revenue amounts are calculated in accordance with GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presentation would become a non-GAAP measure if any of the revenue amounts are adjusted. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant currency presentations are non-GAAP and reconciliation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting financial information in constant currency (isolating exchange rate effects) is a non-GAAP measure under Regulation G/Item 10(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant may comply with reconciliation requirements by presenting historical amounts and constant currency amounts and describing the calculation process and basis of presentation. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Webcast/audio posting condition for Item 2.02 exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: An audio file of an earnings webcast can satisfy the Item 2.02 conditional exemption provided it contains all material financial/statistical information not previously disclosed and investors can access and replay it via the company's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively slides or a similar presentation posted at time of presentation also satisfy the condition. Company must provide all previously undisclosed material financial/statistical information, including Q&A disclosures. Regulation FD may also apply. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for posting information on company's website for oral presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Material financial and other statistical information not previously disclosed that is contained in an oral presentation must appear on the company's website at the time of the presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information disclosed unexpectedly during Q&A must be posted promptly after disclosure. Any Regulation FD requirements must also be satisfied. A webcast suffices. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to furnish an Item 2.02 Form 8-K does not affect Form S-3 eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to furnish an Item 2.02 Form 8-K in a timely manner does not affect a company's eligibility to use Form S-3, because Item 2.02 is a furnishing requirement, not a filing requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, failure to comply with Item 2.02 remains a violation of Section 13(a) of the Exchange Act and related rules. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing earnings release as 10-Q exhibit and reliance on Item 2.02 exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing the earnings release as an exhibit to Form 10-Q prior to a conference call does not preclude relying on the Item 2.02 exemption for the conference call, assuming other Item 2.02 conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer: Yes. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: When earnings release cannot be furnished before conference call
rubrics_metrics.description: If a company issues an earnings release after market close and holds a conference call two hours later and cannot furnish the earnings release on Form 8-K before the call, it cannot rely on the Item 2.02 exemption for the call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The company must furnish the material previously non-public financial/statistical information required by Item 2.02 as an exhibit to a Form 8-K and satisfy other Item 2.02 requirements. A transcript, slides, or similar presentation including such information will satisfy this requirement; all material previously undisclosed financial/statistical information including Q&A must be provided. [Jan. 15, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release announcing results with adjusted earnings falls under Item 2.02
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release announcing quarter results that includes expected adjusted earnings (a non-GAAP financial measure) is subject to Item 2.02 of Form 8-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it contains material, non-public information regarding results of a completed fiscal period, the adjusted earnings range would be subject to Item 2.02 requirements applicable to non-GAAP measures. [Jan. 11, 2010]

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for foreign private issuers when standard-setter expressly permits measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign private issuers may include in filings a non-GAAP financial measure that would otherwise be prohibited by Item 10(e)(1)(ii) if the measure is required or 'expressly permitted' by the standard setter responsible for the GAAP used in the issuer's primary financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Expressly permitted' means the particular measure is clearly and specifically identified as acceptable by that standard setter; it can also be demonstrated by explicit acceptance of the measure. [Jan. 11, 2010]
